say: Welcome to Schönberg Hero. In a few minutes, you'll know how to learn your part for the next concert.
show: Welcome to Schönberg Hero. In a few minutes, you'll know how to learn your part for the next concert.

say: Start with the voice setup. First, type the code your choir gave you. It brings in your programme and your scores. No code? Just practise on your own.
show: Start with the voice setup. First, type the code your choir gave you. It brings in your programme and your scores. No code? Just practise on your own.

say: Then what?
show: Then what?

say: Sing back a little do re mi pattern, one step higher each round, then lower. That's how the app finds where your voice is comfortable. Don't push the top notes.
show: Sing back a little do-re-mi pattern, one step higher each round, then lower. That's how the app finds where your voice is comfortable. Don't push the top notes.

say: What about my Bluetooth earbuds?
show: What about my Bluetooth earbuds?

say: Wired headphones are best. The setup measures any delay: you just sing ta on each click.
show: Wired headphones are best. The setup measures any delay: you just sing “ta” on each click.

say: Now the practice screen. You sing from the sheet music. The blue line is your voice, drawn at the height you sing. Right on the note means in tune; just under it means flat.
show: Now the practice screen. You sing from the sheet music. The blue line is your voice, drawn at the height you sing. Right on the note means in tune; just under it means flat.

say: And if I don't read music?
show: And if I don't read music?

say: Switch to Highway, under Display and tempo. Your notes become bars scrolling toward a line, and you keep the blue line on them. On a laptop, you see the whole choir score, with your line highlighted. On the sheet music, big words above the staff tell you how close you are, from spot on to clearly flat; on the highway, a little bubble does.
show: Switch to “Highway” under Display & tempo. Your notes become bars scrolling toward a line, and you keep the blue line on them. On a laptop, you see the whole choir score, with your line highlighted. On the sheet music, big words above the staff tell you how close you are, from spot on to clearly flat; on the highway, a little bubble does.

say: Every piece is cut into short passages. You practise them level by level, then sing the whole piece through at that level to earn it.
show: Every piece is cut into short passages. You practise them level by level, then sing the whole piece through at that level to earn it.

say: Each level adds one thing, first slow, then in tempo. The notes, on doo, with your part playing. Then the words. Then alone, against the other voices. Then without note names, only the starting chord. And finally by heart, on two different days.
show: Each level adds one thing, first slow, then in tempo. The notes, on “doo”, with your part playing. Then the words. Then alone, against the other voices. Then without note names, only the starting chord. And finally by heart, on two different days.

say: So level three means I'm ready for rehearsal?
show: So level 3 means I'm ready for rehearsal?

say: Once you've sung the whole piece through at level three, yes. Level four means concert ready. A passage slips? Practise just that bit, and the level is yours. Everything right first time? You get a star.
show: Whole piece at level 3 = rehearsal-ready. At level 4 = concert-ready. A passage slips? Practise just that bit, and the level is yours. Everything right first time? You get a star.

say: Can I skip straight to the whole piece?
show: Can I skip straight to the whole piece?

say: Sure. If you know it already, sing it all at any level.
show: Sure. If you know it already, sing it all at any level.

say: And when I mess up?
show: And when I mess up?

say: You see the one note to fix first, and how far off it was, with a tip. One tap loops just that bar, slowly. Then sing the passage again.
show: You see the one note to fix first, and how far off it was, with a tip. One tap loops just that bar, slowly. Then sing the passage again.

say: Today shows a short plan: three or four steps with minutes, paced to your rehearsal and concert. Your week counts practice days, rehearsals too. Ten to fifteen minutes a day is plenty.
show: Today shows a short plan: three or four steps with minutes, paced to your rehearsal and concert. Your week counts practice days, rehearsals too. Ten to fifteen minutes a day is plenty.

say: So, here's what to do right now. One: put on headphones and tap Start voice setup. Two: tap Start today's practice: the app picks your first passage, slow, on doo, with your part playing.

say: That's it?

say: That's it. About ten minutes today. Tomorrow, the Today tab has a new plan.
